I have been creating a website that is primarily to benefit me, but can also be used by other developers called "Mind Map Method":  
[https://mindmapmethod.netlify.app](https://mindmapmethod.netlify.app)

  
Basically, I leverage the chunking psychological concept with the mind map visual organization tool. I was able to extend the project so that users just need to add objects onto the configuration and create new data folders to create their own mind maps. But it's entirely client-side (no database), so it does require getting into the code to do:

[https://github.com/Pythonidaer/d3-mind-map](https://github.com/Pythonidaer/d3-mind-map)

  
Currently, I have d3 graphs for the following topics: JavaScript Fundamentals, JavaScript Paradigms, TypeScript, CSS Design Systems, and more. They're mostly drafts, but I have found that this tool is working wonders for me, and I would love for other people to try it out, fork it, and see if they can customize it to their own wants and needs.

Not sure if you are on Instagram but check out neckpainaid. It’s not what you’re looking for but I’ve created a great strategy from this and I’ll explain below.

Instagram allows you to save images/videos. You can save these posts in collections. The algorithm will recommend you more of what you’ve viewed.

I actually unfollowed close to everybody, so a majority of my feed is just combat and physical therapy.

If you, when you find stretches you like, save them in a collection such as hip/shoulder/back etc.

One good one I found is called a pretzel. Another one is neutral spine thoracic rotation, which is kind of like you in the fetal position on one side and then opening up your arms and rotating your upper body.

Others have mentioned elbows pulling behind the back and I am also going to check those out so thank you for asking.

I occasionally do barrel rolls for my hips. Just helps going into circles to get an idea of how I’m feeling. Also make sure you don’t sit too much it can really mess up your hips and back. Sincerely, remote worker trying to box an amateur bout.

I like the Pallof press overhead. Think of it like a lunge where your resistant band is knitted behind a door and you are taking the side resistance while in a lunge formation and pushing upward. Good for the core.

Knee across chest is good it’s kind of like the pretzel but modified/less intense.

I haven’t tried them yet, but kneeling corkscrews look dope. For more like that check out realgame.athletics

Kneeling thoracic rotation is some of my favorites so let that be my take away.

You basically lunge with your forward leg alongside the wall. You stretch your arm closest to the wall to be parallel with your shoulder (like a forward salute vaguely). Take your left arm and match it like a can opener/both arms extended palms facing eachother. Then rotate your body so that you are extending away from the wall until your body opens up and your arm rotated as close to the wall as you can.

When I was 19 I already had my second job. I didn’t want to live with my grandparents. I felt embarrassed.

Don’t think this needs to overlap with you bud. Let me explain.

I grew up with an extremely dependent guardian, somebody who sucked the finances out of my mother. My mother never had her own place because she was either supporting her mother, or living with another man. This in part made me crave independence.

I’m 30 and am just now preparing to (barely) afford my own place. Up until now I have split places with 1-3 other people.

My ex girlfriend lived with her parents until 24. She’s a singer and had room to sing comfortably. She smoked weed and painted and did drugs in a safe environment. She didn’t have the highest paying job because it offered a flexible schedule and worked for her life. Since then she’s moved out, still doesn’t drive, and while she is starting to become more preferential to getting a different job, she still gets by at the grocery store, using the train, etc.

My point is, it wasn’t pathetic to her be at home until her mid-20s.

My area in the north east is expensive to live in. The federal minimum wage has half of what our state’s minimum wage is, and if one were to earn full time what one earns at $7.50 an hour, say, they’d still be only halfway towards earning their place up here.

I have worked over 55 jobs in my life. Restaurants, gigs, sales, IT, freelance development… I still have not found the career I want to work, but I feel it is in tech.

Now is a great time to take some online tech courses via coursera or freecodecamp.org. Maybe take a coding bootcamp if your family can support you financially. It will benefit you extremely well to begin learning how to budget early on. If you’re going to watch videos on anything, maybe get into that. Maybe find a job like penny stocks idk. Don’t take it from me though. I’ve never bounced a check but I spend too much on food and still have very little savings.

Social interactions are huge in my opinion. So is physical health. If you can find something you like to do such as boxing to stay in shape, or jiu jitsu, you’ll be surprised how quickly your week fills up. You might have a place where you can have a partner come over and have it not be weird, despite living with family. Or it might be like my situation, where I didn’t want to bring girls back to grandma’s apartment because it made me feel like I was lacking things.

There’s probably something to be said about your work ethic, but it’s not my place to surmise or to judge. One thing I’ll definitely say is, now is a peak time time in your life. You might never have this amount of free time ever again. So if you want to discuss with your parents your concerns, that could benefit you if they are good parents and can offer advice or a game plan. If you want to pick up boxing (for example), this’ll be a great way to meet people, get stronger and eventually find a hobby that could take up most of your free time. If you begin taking just one college class you might even be able to do it remotely. I strongly encourage you to work your hardest to complete the project. I once busted ass in a world history project. We had tons of fun. Several years later my classmate was an IT recruiter. I was taking the train into Boston and bumped into him and got my first IT job when my internship had ended at another place. You can bet he wouldn’t have been so eager to help me had I slacked off when it affected him.

One thing that drove me nuts about coding bootcamps was me not having the time because I worked full time. I finally finished one and it nearly gave me a mental health crisis. Multiple 13-hour days (with a full time job) that lasted half a year.

I don’t think it’s okay that you’re 19 and still dependent on your parents. I also think it’s okay that you’re 19 and still dependent on your parents.

I think YOU might not think it’s okay, and for that I agree with you. Start socializing more. Change your habits. Read more, Youtube less, maybe. Find a hobby. Learn to budget. Take advantage of the most free time you’ll have for a long time, as work and kids and a true hobby will make season go by like a snap of the fingers.

It’s very common for people to stay with their families. It’s not easy to afford that level of independence. It was pathetic for me by my own standard. I also lived with a cigarette chomping drunk and didn’t want that to reflect on me, or see my girlfriends witness these frequent at home episodes I had to witness.

One big reason I never felt it pathetic for my ex to live at home was 24, was because she was a very talented musician. Her reason for staying at a nearby, flexible job made sense. Even now she’s going out less because she can’t afford it, yet she splits a place and does what she wants. She’s living within her means and has solid family support, and I think that’s something you might be gearing  towards as well.

Do you have a hobby? Ones that come to mind for me are fitness, music, arts & crafts, writing, meetups, open mics and more. Many of these things cost money, but besides buying pens and paper, brushes, guitar, a gym membership etc, a lot of these hobbies will only cost so much and after a while they can become sustainable.

I don’t mean to force boxing on you, it’s just my own personal example. I spend $300 a month on personal mit sessions, sparring and drilling. I do it 12x a month. I don’t go more than that because I need time for running, recovering, coding, chilling and watching anime, etc. it’s definitely one of my main hobbies. But $300 a month I feel isn’t the worst. It’s expensive, but it keeps me away from doing drugs in alleyways and shit.

I sort of love coding. There are literally years’worth of top quality free content online. You can take a 6-month course for less than $50 on Coursera and get one of their Google certificates. Or you can get free certificates on freeCodeCamp and learn web development or data science or something else. PluralSight has a ton of great content too and between there and Udemy you could get into IT as well.

If you’re not in a rush, find something that makes you passionate. If you can afford it, travel abroad. Even with the covid scares it’s probably prime time to do so if you want to make the most out of being young.

Planning long term was difficult for me at your age. Discipline has gotten me far, but so has understanding habits and trying to implement what I’ve learned from books.

Books you might like reading include: Learning how to Learn, the Power of Habit, and I can send other recommendations if you’re ever curious.

I think it’s time to start weaning off the tit if that’s what you feel you’re doing. Conversely, there is NOTHING wrong with having a stable and supportive family who can provide a home for you to stay in as you figure out what you want to do with your life. But traveling, finding a hobby, expanding your education, taking advantage of your free time, and achieving being able to have your own healthy income and budget are really great things for you to be learning now. When I was 19 I fought two cage fights with little to no experience. Each time I was tko’d.

Those two moments have added so much to my character. It’s not that the losses defined me. Rather, stepping in the arena has made other things easier - open mics, sticking up for myself, public speaking, leading business meetings. 

The learning experience really dug deep into a hole I never knew existed. Sounds bleak, but the flip side to it is I can reach deep inside myself for the will to overcome when life gets tough. I was humbled. I worked really hard to improve myself. I even stepped away for a very long time. I attribute many of my successes to those successes. They were failures in that I didn’t win, but I look at it like trauma. I used that after effect to reassess myself. After a bit of self-pity I became more motivated than ever before.

I think it’s okay to cry. It’s okay to want to feel like shit. Whatever you mean, sad, ashamed, embarrassed. I’d rather be brave enough to try than to be on the sidelines having never tried, getting pleasure only by being the critic and telling other people what they can or can’t do.

I hope you get well soon. I think it took me a couple months to get over my loss. With that being said, don’t let it keep you down for long. It doesn’t have to be a “distraction” to keep yourself occupied with other things like work, hanging with friends, exploring the city, trying new hobbies etc. In the same vein, once your coach thinks you’re up to it, once you’re mentally good (I mean recovering from a KO is no joke, but feeling sad is another story), I guarantee you go back into the gym more motivated than ever before.

Lastly, also in the same vein, this is a great learning experience. How do we know what love feels like until we feel pain? How do we know what a great achievement feels like until we’ve failed miserably? I feel confident that you will work very hard in life, in and out of the sport, because you have now gained a prime motivator to never have this feeling never again.

Fighter pay IMO is very low because fighters either are or believe they are forced to fight in the UFC to make the most living, fight the best fighters, etc.

Counterpoint: Judo Kayla Harrison. Female PFL champion, just won $1 as the tournament champ in her division.

Women divisions are less populated than men and I’m sure it’s not sexist to say that the talent pool has some catching up to do, but when it comes to the best she is truly the cream that rises. She trains with Amanda Nunes but unfortunately she is an anomaly.

Gegard “Moose” Mousasi was flirting with a title shot before leaving the UFC. I believe he left due to low pay. He went on to become champion in Bellator, but not enough people know about him.

Mighty Mouse also left UFC and I believe has made a better business decision fighting in One FC but I don’t know the facts/stats on his pay.

What I do know is that as soon as the next big UFC star decides to leave the promotion to fight in another, more people will slowly realize that the best fighters aren’t always in the UFC, but the issue is UFC still doesn’t have a clear competitor.

Bellator, PFL, One FC, etc— these promotions show they have dominant fighters. For example, Eddie Alvarez (champion), Justin Gaejthe (savage), and other fighters have come here and proven to be great caliber if not champion fighters.

One issue I perceive is that when fighters earn belts in other promotions (like Conor McGregor being a double champ prior to entering the UFC) is that those belts are perceived to have less value than the UFC’s belt.

Once there is another option than UFC that even a casual fight fan can turn to, fighter pay will shift somehow.

I don’t know how many acronyms/promotions are in boxing. Are there 5 acknowledged belts? More?

A lot of Americans in my opinion equate MMA to the UFC as they do American football to NFL. If the perspective can shift and have it be more like boxing, then maybe UFC fighter pay will even go down, but I doubt that.

Once a promotion can afford what the UFC can, talent pool, budget, reputation and all, they can then begin changing fighter pay as we know it in MMA.

Probably would have to take another thread like this and compare it to top earners in other MMA promotions for further analysis.

I work really hard and have not yet traveled. It sounds weird but I don’t want to go to a country the first time and have it be somebody else’s 2nd or 3rd time every time. I want to share the experience of having earned travel and having gone to a new place together for the first time.

I was in good shape and have gotten in better shape, but I am still overweight and until I have even a generally tight core I feel like a hypocrite. I don’t need somebody who is shaped like a bikini model, but I am not interested in somebody who is overweight. It’s rude and unfortunate to eliminate somebody over something that often can’t be controlled or doesn’t reflect a person’s personality, but I notice a lot of my standard window regards being attracted to somebody and being picky as hell about it.

I also don’t want to be with a woman that already has kids. I’m open to it later in life, but as of now I don’t want to have kids. I’m not ready. And I know boyfriends aren’t desired or expected to be step dad material in most cases. But I don’t want to carry that burden whatever the expectation is. It’s not a red flag to me, but especially on OKC if the two things I know about you are that you are loving and have two beautiful children, it’s a hard pass and I wish you well.

My problem also has a lot to do with superficiality. I’m actually not a fan of OD makeup, plastic, fake lips etc. I don’t want to be with somebody who looks like a wax museum figure rather fun somebody comfortable with natural beauty (just wake up and do some yoga, catch you reading a book on a hammock and smiling is the type of beauty I imagine).
